note: THE CHAIN LEDGER for the speedrun route's leg entrances.
Each entry records the observed EXIT state of one route leg (route id
all-sf3-bn4-first, legs derived in sim/route-legs.ts).
A leg is ONE BitNode completion (bn4.3 is the third completion of BN4,
entered holding SF4.2), so a leg's goal exit IS the next leg's entrance.
A leg's measured exit intelligence becomes the NEXT leg's entrance
intelligence -- deriveRouteLegs prefers these numbers over the
+10-per-completion estimate. Source-File entrances are never recorded
here: they are fully determined by the route order.
SHAPE. `legs` is keyed by leg name, and each entry is:
"bn4.1": { "exit": { "intelligenceAtGoal": 12 }, "note": "..." }
`intelligenceAtGoal` is the only key read (sim/profiles.ts); everything
else is for humans. A route-leg run prints `exit intelligence: <n>` and
records it in sim.result as strategy.actualSkills.intelligence.
Recording here is what makes a measurement STICK: a completed leg also
mints the next leg's checkpoint with its observed exit baked in, but that
is one blob from one seed. Only an entry below moves the profiles.
RULES.
1. Record only from a run you actually observed, on the leg's own profile
(bun run sim --profile leg-bn<node>.<level> --compact), taken at the
run's goal. A horizon exit is not a goal exit; do not record it.
2. Updating a leg's exit changes every downstream leg's entrance and
therefore its scenario fingerprint. That is the chain working as
designed: re-measure downstream legs afterwards, in order.
3. `provenance` pins the simulator semantics, exactly as in bn1.json.
Bumping SIMULATOR_MODEL_VERSION or the vendored commit obliges
re-measuring the whole chain before recording new exits.

provenance.recordedFrom: re-pinned at model 11 (sim/fidelity.ts) after the BN4 leg-1 pass. Three defects fixed, all outside BN4 and all affecting every leg: a seeded-stream leak (initTelemetry drew from Math.random, which the simulator seeds, so telemetry-on and --perf runs of one seed diverged completely -- recorded evidence is all --perf and therefore unmoved); an ns-proxy deadlock (a guaranteeFit union asked for less than it demanded and priced unpriceable names at the 80 GB fallback, so the resident demanded 162.1 GB, was offered 65.6 GB twelve thousand times, and the controller silently stopped at 21-24h); and DarknetMoneyMultiplier read from the SF5-gated getter rather than the static table. Still no exits measured: leg-bn4.1 now runs its whole horizon but does not reach its goal (sim/tests/baselines/bn4.json), so every leg entrance remains the estimate.
